DDX HY Patterns

How to use this page

  1. Pathology → Path Overview: the detailed view, one card per disease. Read the one-line mechanism, then open the card for pathophysiology, presentation, diagnosis, treatment, HY notes, traps and buzzwords. Answer the four recall checks out loud before you reveal them.
  2. Pathology → Path Table: the condensed high-yield chart for each category, one row per disease. Click a disease name to jump to its card. Turn on Cover names or cover a column and rebuild it from memory.
  3. DDX: the cross-cutting high-yield patterns (one toggle per pattern) and the side-by-side comparison tables of look-alikes.
  4. Practice Qs → Practice DDX: 50 rapid-fire clue sets. Name the disease in under 10 seconds.
  5. Practice Qs → Practice MCQs: 49 Step 1–style vignettes with the explanation and the trap. Aim for 90% before the exam.
  6. The Diseases list, search, category menus and Exam topics filter both Pathology views at once.
Step 1 high yieldMost immunology questions turn on one discriminator: which arm is missing (B cell, T cell, phagocyte or complement), which hypersensitivity type is at work (I–IV), or which autoantibody is present. Name the defect first, then predict the infections, labs and biopsy findings.
Yellow = high yield STEP 1board fact beyond the lecture (First Aid, UWorld, Bootcamp, Physeo) UWorldtopic has a UWorld learning objective EXAMflagged "on exam" in the student exam guide
